_note: Corrections to tricks the book got wrong, keyed by slug and merged over the
PDF extract field by field. tricks.json is rewritten wholesale every time the
book is re-read, so a correction made there would not survive; this is where
Only list the fields that are actually wrong: everything else keeps coming
from the book, so a later re-extraction still improves those. Never override
name, page or pdfPage. The slug comes from the name and a user's saved stars
are keyed by it, and the page reference has to keep pointing at the page the
corrected is shown on the entry, because the linked PDF page still carries
the old description and a silent contradiction is worse than a stated one.

rubik-s-cube.corrected: The book has this as one turn on each axis: flip, flat yaw, roll. It is a 180 flip, a full roll held inverted, then a second 180 flip the same way.
rubik-s-cube.howto: A forward 180 flip to inverted, a full 360 roll held there, then a second forward 180 flip the same way round and back upright. Both flips go forward and both go the same way, which is what makes this one continuous puzzle rather than a flip and a roll flown back to back. The quad is inverted for the whole of the roll, and that is the part that catches people out: the roll has to be flown upside down, on a line, without the flip either side of it drifting.
mastery: Flip, roll and flip again without falling out of it.
Both flips the same way, the roll clean and inverted.
Seamless Rubik's Cube, one line, no pause between the three.
steps: Snap a forward 180 flip, to inverted
Hold it there and roll a full 360
Another forward 180 the same way, back upright
prereqs: Clean flips and rolls on their own
rubik-s-cube.practice: Open air with height to spare, because the middle of this is flown upside down. Get the inverted roll on its own first: half flip, roll, half flip back, slowly. Then join them up. Keeping both flips going the same way is the whole trick; taking the second one back the way you came is a different, easier move.
mistakes: Taking the second flip back the other way, which undoes it rather than completing it
Rolling before the first flip has finished, so the roll is not truly inverted
Drifting off line through the inverted roll
Losing height in the middle and running out of room for the second flip

cubik-s-rube.corrected: The book has this as one turn on each axis: roll, flat yaw, flip. It is a 180 roll, a full flip held inverted, then a second 180 roll the same way.
cubik-s-rube.howto: The Rubik's Cube with the axes swapped. A 180 roll to inverted, a forward 360 flip held there, then a second 180 roll the same way round and back upright. Same shape, same rhythm, the other axis doing the work. As with the Rubik's Cube, both outer turns go the same way: rolling back the way you came is a different move.
mastery: Roll, flip and roll again without falling out of it.
Both rolls the same way, the flip clean and inverted.
Seamless Cubik's Rube, one line, no pause between the three.
steps: Hold it there and flip a forward 360
Another 180 roll the same way, back upright
prereqs: Clean rolls and flips on their own
cubik-s-rube.practice: Same drill as the Rubik's Cube, the other way up. Half roll, flip, half roll back, slowly, with height to spare. The inverted flip is the part to get comfortable with before you try to run the three together.
mistakes: Taking the second roll back the other way, which undoes it rather than completing it
Starting the flip before the roll has finished
Drifting off line through the inverted flip
Losing height in the middle and running out of room for the second roll
